_comment: Intended instruction-count changes between the merge-base and this branch head, each with its measured values and its cause. tools/check_instruction_counts.py accepts an out-of-tolerance operation ONLY if it appears here with matching numbers, and fails on an entry that no longer applies -- so this file cannot become a blanket exemption. An entry whose change the merge-base already contains (the reference measures its 'to': the state of every entry here once this branch merges) is reported as landed and excuses nothing; it stays true until its operation moves again. Same shape as benchmarks/check_baseline_justification.py requires of the wall-clock floors. Re-measured 2026-11-06 (AGENTS.md section 6.6): ubuntu-latest moved to 26.04 and gcc 15, which moved every absolute count, so every entry recorded on gcc 13.3 described neither side of the A/B comparison. Every number below is a measurement on the toolchain named in measured_on; the gcc 13.3 figures are kept beside each entry for the record and are not read by the gate.
measured_on: the ubuntu-latest (26.04) toolchain: gcc 15.2.0-16ubuntu1, cmake 4.2.3-2ubuntu2, valgrind 3.26.0, in a resolute chroot; trees without the x86-64 baseline pin built with -march=x86-64-v3 to reproduce the runner's amd64v3 compiler default; Release static library with LTO, driver -O2, AMA_DISPATCH_NO_AUTOTUNE=1, difference method at N=10; x86-64 host with AVX2/BMI2/ADX/VAES/VPCLMULQDQ/SHA-NI/AVX-512, dispatch fingerprint 'arch=x86-64 sha3=AVX2 kyber=AVX2 dilithium=AVX2 sphincs=AVX2 aes_gcm=AVX2 ed25519=Generic C chacha20poly1305=AVX2 argon2=AVX2 x25519=AVX2'. Calibrated before use: 702e253 measured here reproduced the runner's own A/B measurement of 702e253 (run 42244243340) on 17 of 18 operations exactly and ed25519_sign within 4 Ir (0.001%)

aes_256_gcm_encrypt.reason: Secret-operand gate cures, paid for in instructions: the AES-GCM partial-block and round-key changes that keep secret state out of FP-domain moves, the value barriers on secret scalar loops, and AMA_API's zero_call_used_regs("all") epilogue on every exported call (register-residue fix, INVARIANT-6). The string-op header removed the fortified __memcpy_chk calls, which recovers part of it. Measured by the runner's own A/B job on fbefa4c (job 128690957185), merge-base c0f2254, gcc 15.2 on ubuntu-latest; values are the runner's.

supersedes.reason: This branch pins the x86-64 ISA baseline (-march=x86-64 -mtune=generic) in CMakeLists.txt. The reference, 702e253, is built by the runner's Ubuntu 26.04 amd64v3 gcc 15, which defaults to x86-64-v3, so its non-kernel code -- the portable paths the dispatcher selects on a host WITHOUT AVX2 -- carried AVX2, VEX and BMI1/BMI2 instructions: tools/check_avx_scoping.py found them in 449 non-kernel symbols. With the pin that code is compiled for baseline x86-64 again, so it retires more instructions; the CPUID-gated kernels keep their per-file flags and are unchanged. This is the cost of the correction, not a regression: the higher count is the code a pre-AVX2 host can execute.

Security hardening, paid for in instructions. The AES-256 key schedule and the GHASH accumulator are scrubbed at exit where gcc -O3 had hoisted them somewhere the source never named (INVARIANT-6), and the AEAD accept/reject return is masked rather than branched, pinned by an instruction-invariance gate.

chacha20poly1305_encrypt.reason: The ChaCha20 x8 kernel re-broadcasts its initial rows from general registers at the add-back and stores each transposed half at once (no FP-domain spill under clang), and every exported call clears its call-clobbered registers on return (AMA_API, INVARIANT-6). The key words are loaded through value barriers after this measurement; that moves the count by well under the 2% tolerance. Measured by the runner's own A/B job on fbefa4c (job 128690957185), merge-base c0f2254, gcc 15.2 on ubuntu-latest; values are the runner's.

This entry supersedes this operation's 5.0.0 entry, kept in full under 'supersedes': a DECLARED BREAKING CHANGE, not a performance regression -- ama_dilithium_sign moved from ML-DSA.Sign_internal (FIPS 204 Algorithm 7) to the Sec 5.2 external interface, which changes mu, so 4.x signatures do not verify under 5.0.0.

DECLARED BREAKING CHANGE, not a performance regression. ama_dilithium_sign moved from ML-DSA.Sign_internal (FIPS 204 Algorithm 7, mu = H(tr || M), no domain separator) to the Sec 5.2 EXTERNAL interface (Algorithm 2), which prepends 0x00 || len(ctx) || ctx. That changes mu, which changes every rejection-sampling decision, so the loop runs a different number of times for any given key and message. Verified by measurement: the same seed yields an IDENTICAL public key on both sides but different signatures, and each side rejects the other's -- head sig VALID under head and INVALID under main, main sig VALID under main and INVALID under head. 4.x signatures do not verify under 5.0.0; this is the correction that makes the library interoperable with liboqs, BoringSSL, Go and Bouncy Castle. See CHANGELOG.md's BREAKING entry. The internal interface (Algorithms 7 and 8) is no longer exported: it is ama_ml_dsa_sign_internal() / ama_ml_dsa_verify_internal(), compiled only into the AMA_TESTING_MODE archive (src/c/internal/ama_testing_exports.h). Corrected 2026-09-24 (AGENTS.md 6.6): this entry named ama_ml_dsa_sign(), which no longer exists.

supersedes.reason: INVARIANT-51: the signer derives A = [a]B and refuses a key whose stored public half disagrees (2026-09 audit, B-2). Signing therefore does TWO fixed-base scalar multiplications where it did one -- the check is the same operation that computes R -- and that is the whole of the +103,629 Ir. Deliberate: without it, two signatures over ONE message under two different stored halves share R and give s1 - s2 = (h1 - h2) * a mod L, which recovers the private scalar, and a caller that stores the halves separately or rebuilds a key from a corrupted record reaches that input with no fault injector. The comparison itself is a laundered mask rather than a branch, so the output is masked and the verdict selected without a conditional -- worth about 130 Ir against the branching form CI measured at 331,941 on 84ad90d2, and it is what keeps ed25519-sign in the secret-taint lane that runs against the shipped shared object, where a declassification point expands to nothing. Supersedes the -9.32% entry, which described the Ed25519 rewrite before the check existed; that rewrite's saving is still in this number, under the doubled work.
